backups.docsSelectHint: Pick a topic from the left side.
backups.docsGettingStartedBody:
1. Open the Files live tab and check agent status.
2. When status is Indexing or Backing up, wait for cycle completion.
3. After completion you should see file rows and updated timestamps.
backups.docsAgentStatusBody:
Indexing: agent scans files and refreshes index.
Backing up: agent packages and uploads data.
Index ready: cycle finished, waiting for next scan.
Waiting for configuration: verify agent settings.
backups.docsTroubleshootingBody:
No signal: confirm agent process is running and can reach buffer.
No files: confirm backup roots are configured.
Stale status: check upload/log-ingest tokens and server_id match.
backups.inventoryRootsEmpty: No roots reported yet — the agent sends them each backup cycle.
backups.inventoryFilesEmpty: No indexed files yet — wait for the agent scan.
backups.inventoryEmptySnaps: No sealed packages yet for this root.
backups.inventoryArchiveHint: Very large roots may seal long after files change — future manifest-at-seal will tie each file to a package precisely.

addServer.title: Add machine
addServer.intro: Name this machine (e.g. Raspberry Pi, VPS). On the host, run the agent JAR — in the GUI you’ll set buffer URL and paste the token (same as in the browser, no manual CLI required).
addServer.adminHint: As administrator you may issue activation for any user — the machine lands on their list.
addServer.tokenReadyBody: The token is valid for 24 hours and can only be used once.
addServer.keyHeading: Key to paste in the agent
addServer.cliGui: On a machine with JRE (simplest — GUI):
addServer.jarNote: The JAR file name may differ — use the one from the ProperBackup release (multi‑MB). Do not use original-….jar from the build.
addServer.macNote: On macOS use ProperBackup Agent.app from the release, or ProperBackup-Agent-macos.command / fat JAR in the same folder.
addServer.afterNoteRich: After successful activation the agent saves configuration and may open the panel in your browser. The machine appears on the owner’s list — active tokens are also under **Active tokens**.
addServer.clipboardBody:
ProperBackup — agent activation (Windows / macOS / Linux; JRE 21+):

macOS: easiest is ProperBackup Agent.app from the release (bundled runtime, no JDK install).
Or use ProperBackup-Agent-macos.command / java -jar with the fat JAR.
Do not run original-….jar — that thin build artefact lacks libraries.

1) Recommended: GUI wizard
   java -jar properbackup-agent.jar --gui
   Paste the token below and adjust buffer URL if needed.

2) Or from terminal:
   java -jar properbackup-agent.jar --activate {{token}}

Key (for GUI):
{{token}}

wizard.title: Data recovery
wizard.step1Body: We download the first 49 bytes of the encrypted object and verify your password locally — without pulling the full archive yet.
wizard.step2Body: Local mock thaws in ~5 seconds. Against OVH Cloud Archive in production — about 4 hours.
wizard.localDecryptBody: Decryption happens in your browser via Web Crypto API. Your password never leaves this device.
